concept.name: Responsive buying
concept.definition: In Market Profile/auction terminology, responsive buying is buying that appears below the established value area — the 'expected' behavior of buyers responding to prices that are cheap relative to accepted value. Responsive buying is what defends value area lows and rotates a balanced market back toward the point of control.
concept.intuition: Responsive buyers are bargain hunters: they step in when price gets cheap relative to where the market agreed value lies.
concept.mechanics: Identified by buying activity at/below the prior VAL, typically with the opposite conviction signature of initiative trade — rotations rather than range extension — and read as range-maintaining behavior favoring mean-reversion tactics back toward the POC.
concept.failure_modes: Responsive buying fails precisely when it matters most — on the day balance breaks and initiative selling takes over below value, buying 'cheap' prices is buying a falling market.
concept.misconceptions: Responsive buying at a low is not a bottom signal; it describes the behavioral category of the flow, and its continuation depends on the balance persisting.
concept.example: Price dips below yesterday's VAL to 4,496, buyers appear and rotate the market back to the POC at 4,515 by midday — textbook responsive buying maintaining the range.

citations.source: FuturesIndicators — Trading With Market Profile: Practical Setups (responsive buying below the value area)
